chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:
In the wisdom of the family of Dāwūd, it is fitting for the wise person to be devoted to his own affair, guarding his tongue, and knowing the people of his time.

key_terms.أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ: the people of one’s own time and social context
key_terms.حَافِظًا لِلِسَانِهِ: guarding one’s speech from improper words
key_terms.حِكْمَةِ آلِ دَاوُدَ: the inherited wisdom associated with the family of Dāwūd

ai.seo_question: What qualities should a wise person have according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a concise ethical teaching attributed to the wisdom of the family of Dāwūd. It describes the qualities of an intelligent person as attending to his own concerns, restraining his speech, and understanding the people and conditions of his time.
